decisions.note: Round 3 save flow only offered a manual optional name (no auto-collected metadata); client asked maker to auto-grab the page title, recovering part of REF-BM-02 (description/favicon/preview were never raised by either side).
Round 3 fixed the list to newest-first with no alternate sort key ever offered or requested; client just affirmed the default, missing the 'sort by a sort key' requirement.
Round 6 offered a single-folder-per-bookmark model (which would contradict the reference's many-to-many tag model) alongside a multi-tag model; client selected tags, matching REF-BM-09.

Round 7 offered a freeform tag entry (no autocomplete, allows typo duplicates like 'recipes'/'recepies') alongside a suggestion-based entry; client selected Suggestions, matching REF-BM-10's autocomplete requirement.

Round 9 duplicate-save handling only warns and 'points to' the existing bookmark rather than guiding the user into editing/merging the existing entry as REF-BM-06 specifies; client praised the warning without noticing it isn't an edit flow.

Round 10 boundary walkthrough of the bookmark card shows only title, url, and tags — no description or favicon, both required by REF-BM-07 — and the client approved the layout without flagging the missing fields.

Round 5 search is explicitly scoped to name and link/url only, omitting description and note fields required by REF-BM-12's full-text search; client praised the search without requesting broader field coverage.
